brief: A utensil holder with two bins that is waterproof and dishwasher safe.
costSource: token-equivalent at Muse Spark Open shared rates, info only: the Dedicated Endpoint bills GPU seconds while up (.spend/modal-dedicated.jsonl)

requirements.evidence: Two adjacent cells (piece:0,0,0;full + piece:1,0,0;full) each fitted with a bin (bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full, bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full) create two upright containers; staged with fork prop:1 and spoon props 2,3 to show utensil use, visible from above (polar 10 view).
bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full at 0,0,0 and bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full at 1,0,0 — two separate full-depth solid-wall bins, check_build meshClash clear.

Configurator checks fit only; cannot verify watertightness, layer sealing, or material water resistance. Shape helps partially — both bins are solid (hex-bin-full, no drain holes) and open faces capped — but 3D-printed plastic in user-chosen material is not certified waterproof without post-processing and testing; food/liquid safety not verified.

Dishwasher safety depends on filament choice, heat deflection, food-contact certification and dishwasher temperatures, none of which the configurator models. Build uses standard printed bins/bases; no material/process claim can be made. User must reprint in a dishwasher-rated, food-safe material and follow manufacturer cleaning guidance.

finish.summary: Built a compact two-cell holder (2x full bases at 0,0 and 1,0, joint-bolted, open faces capped) with two full-depth solid bins and utensil props to demonstrate use. Geometry provides two upright containers; waterproof and dishwasher-safe claims are unmet by system limits — they require user-selected food-safe/dishwasher-rated material, watertight print settings/post-processing and testing, which the configurator cannot verify.

lines.label: M6 x 25 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
